extracted.intended_audience: naturalists, scientific travelers, and educated readers interested in physical geography and the scientific method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for observing, measuring, and generalizing in natural philosophy and physical geography, especially from travel and field observations in varied climates and mountain regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze individuality of objects and diversity of forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace different sources of impressions by analyzing the individuality of objects and the diversity of forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic analysis of individual objects and the various forces producing impressions is necessary to resolve the unity and diversity of phenomena; this analytic approach helps distinguish causes of impressions and emotions produced by nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use graphic delineations arranged systematically
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic delineations of nature, arranged according to systematic views, both please the imagination and indicate grades of impressions (from uniform sea-shore to fertile torrid zones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly considered illustrations or systematic representations can show successive grades of phenomena and should complement verbal or numerical descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer accurate trigonometrical and barometrical measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevations and geographic data should be based on accurate trigonometrical or barometrical measurements rather than crude estimates or reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Chimborazo's elevation relies on trigonometrical measurement; the Dhawalagiri elevation depends on unsettled elements like azimuths and latitudes. The text warns that erroneous numbers appear in maps due to incorrect reductions—favor primary, precise methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confound calculations with actual measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid substituting simple or theoretical calculations where actual field measurements are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humboldt criticizes conflating calculated 'mean' elevations or isolated summit heights with directly measured plateau elevations; he urges re-investigation by travelers who can judge land conformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine numerous data sources and critically revise hypsometrical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive conclusions from the combination of numerous data furnished by different observers and subject hypsometrical (height) data to critical revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elevation and snow-line conclusions should be drawn from multiple travellers' barometrical, trigonometrical, and observational data and must be critically re-evaluated where discrepancies exist (e.g., differing snow-line elevations on Himalayan slopes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between sporadic observations and maxima/limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between sporadic occurrences (e.g., isolated snowfalls) and the actual maximums or limits (e.g., true snow-line height).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travelers often confuse sporadic snow with the highest extent of the snow-line; careful distinction and appropriate definition of the measured quantity are required for accurate physical geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for geographic position when interpreting phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that geographic position (latitude, proximity to seas or plateaus) crucially affects the variety and character of natural phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Himalaya's geographic position limits tropical vegetation there despite high elevation; the juxtaposition of climates in equatorial mountain chains affords unique opportunities to observe many vegetation zones in small areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use numerical calculation and computation to demonstrate regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit observed regularities (e.g., in climate or atmospheric variation with altitude) to numerical calculation and computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invariability of certain atmospheric and celestial laws can and should be demonstrated quantitatively—Humboldt points to tables of temperature vs altitude and suggests these laws are amenable to computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vicious empiricism and imperfect inductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject empiricism based on inaccurate or imperfect observations that produce false inductions and popular prejudices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical philosophy grounded on poor observation perpetuates error; scientists must doubt, investigate, and distinguish between certain and probable conclusions rather than multiply exceptions or cling to poorly observed axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation must be aided by reason to seek causes and generalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation, when combined with reason, should trace phenomena to their causes and strive to generalize, extending the circle of observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is not merely to collect unconnected observations but to seek causal relationships and broader laws; generalization strengthens theory and the understanding of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice patient, repeated, and precise measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve precision through patient repetition and meticulous measurement across scales (from micrometer measurements to meridian altitudes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include use of heliometers, meridian altitude measures, and persistent telescopic searches; such painstaking work underpins reliable scientific conclusions and 'higher views of the laws of the universe.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent methods to corroborate findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Corroborate results with independent measurement techniques (e.g., trigonometrical, barometrical, boiling-point determinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humboldt cites barometrical observations, boiling-point-based elevation estimates, and trigonometrical measures as mutually supportive approaches; where methods disagree, further investigation is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select observers experienced in judging land conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer data and re-investigation by travelers accustomed to judge the general conformation of the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humboldt calls for experienced field observers to revisit and correct hypsometrical and climatic conclusions, since superficial or unskilled travelers may introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize prior research and references when deriving conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Base deductions on a synthesis of earlier works, observations, and published memoirs rather than isolated reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author repeatedly integrates findings from Webb, Gerard, Herbert, Moorcroft, Pentland, Jacquemont, and others to build more reliable conclusions; thorough citation and combination of sources is essential.
